audit.note: the context-menu toggle's pressed state travels with its press event

deviations.what: The two menu-entry toggles need no handler at all: each ToggleButton's pressed and the Table property it drives (enableColumnFreeze / enableCellFilter) bind the SAME field on the one default model, which is exactly what the original's two-way {ui>/showFreezeMenuEntry} and {ui>/enableCellFilter} bindings do - only the `ui>` prefix is dropped. The THIRD toggle (onToggleContextMenu) does round-trip, because what it switches is a SUBTREE of the view and not a property; see the context-menu deviation.

Two of the three CONTROLLER-BUILT menus are still dropped; the third is ported since 2026-08-26. (a) associateHeaderMenus creates a sap.m.table.columnmenu.Menu and associates it with the name/productId/quantity columns via setHeaderMenu. This used to be called "a control-returning factory, the capability boundary CAPABILITIES marks as not expressible", and that was wrong twice: there is no factory - onInit builds TWO menus ONCE and statically (an EMPTY new ColumnMenu() for name and productId, and one new ColumnMenu({items: [ActionItem, ActionItem]}) with two fixed entries for quantity) - and Column headerMenu is a plain ASSOCIATION taking a control id, not an aggregation of built controls. The real obstacle is VERSION: sap.ui.table.Column headerMenu is @since 1.110 and sap.m.table.columnmenu.Menu is @since 1.110 too, so keeping them is a POST_171 decision that would move this class out of src/01, and onQuantitySort's this.byId('table').sort( oColumn, sOrder, bAdd ) additionally wants a COLUMN INSTANCE as its first argument, which the control-call wire casts to a string. It is a decision left open, not an impossibility. (b) onToggleContextMenu builds a sap.m.Menu with two bound MenuItems and hands it to setContextMenu / destroyContextMenu. This used to say "an aggregation of controls built at runtime has no bindable equivalent either", which was false: the sap.ui.table.Table contextMenu aggregation is @since 1.54 - BELOW the 1.71 floor - and app 436 has been porting exactly this shape on sap.m.Tree. The port now does the same: the toggle's pressed state travels on a round trip and the backend emits the contextMenu > m:Menu > two m:MenuItem subtree ({NAME} and {PRODUCTID}, the original's {Name}/{ProductId}) or leaves it out, which is setContextMenu / destroyContextMenu. (c) onProductIdCellContextMenu is still dropped, and with it the Table's beforeOpenContextMenu attribute: it calls oEvent.preventDefault( ), builds a sap.ui.unified.Menu per cell and opens it docked to the clicked cell's DOM ref with Popup.Dock - a DOM anchor and a per-cell veto the wire has no counterpart for. Its handler goes with it. The columns, their sortProperty/filterProperty and the table's own header menus are unaffected. One waiver rides with (b): the two MenuItem texts are RELATIVE bindings on a control the linter sees no binding context for, so both lines carry an abap2ui5lint-disable-next-line for relative-binding-without-context. It is a static blind spot, not a broken binding - sap.ui.table's _MenuUtils._openCustomContentCellContextMenu does oContextMenu.setBindingContext( TableUtils.getBindingContextOfRow( oRow ), ... ) before it opens the menu, which is why the original binds {Name} and {ProductId} there in the first place.

The shared 123-row demo ProductCollection (sap/ui/demo/mock/products.json) is inlined with the five columns the sample binds. The original computes DeliveryDate from Date.now() with an i-mod-10 offset in 4-day steps; a fixed base date (2026-07-23) is used here so the port is deterministic - the corpus convention of app 164. The Quantity and Delivery Date columns keep the original's typed complex bindings with the path switched to the ABAP field, and sortProperty/filterProperty carry the ABAP (upper-cased) field names. ProductPicUrl values point at the OpenUI5 host per the asset-URL rule.

The footer OverflowToolbar stays empty: onInit lazily requires sap/ui/table/sample/TableExampleUtils and appends a ToolbarSpacer plus its createInfoButton( ) to it. That helper lives in the demo kit's own sample folder, not in any UI5 library, and only opens a popover pointing at the sample's source. Every sap.ui.table sample of this batch drops it the same way.

The sample's asset paths are host-absolutized. The demo kit serves them relative (test-resources/...), which an abap2UI5 app has no document root to resolve against, so the port points at https://sdk.openui5.org/... instead. The values are otherwise the mock's own. Declared 2026-08-21 for consistency, and RE-COUNTED 2026-08-23: the sentence used to claim the rewrite was 'declared by all 77 ports that do it', which had stopped being true as the corpus grew past that day's snapshot - 126 ports do it now, and 17 of them declared it nowhere. Those 17 carry the declaration since today, so the claim holds again; a stale absolute count is what made it wrong, so this wording names the date the count was taken.
